primitives.name: Cache Model Selector
primitives.verbatim_quote: The decision that frames everything: which caching model is your app on?
primitives.assumptions: App must choose one of two mutually exclusive caching models: previous (default) or Cache Components (opt-in).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Build-time error if both models are mixed.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's binary classification of data freshness regimes (static vs dynamic) and GSE's routing state machine transitions.

primitives.name: Fetch Tag Invalidator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `revalidateTag('slate')` — purges all fetches tagged `'slate'`, then each tagged fetch revalidates individually; stale data is served in the meantime (stale-while-revalidate).
primitives.assumptions: All fetches with matching tags are invalidated and revalidated asynchronously.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Stale-while-revalidate regime where stale data serves until fresh fetch completes.

layer2.mapping: Acts as kernel for GSI's event-driven update logic; GSE uses it to trigger state transitions in component hierarchies.
layer2.telemetry: Observable via network logs showing tag-based fetch purges and revalidations.

primitives.name: Route Dynamic Poison
primitives.verbatim_quote: - If **any** fetch in the route uses `revalidate: 0` or `cache: 'no-store'`, the **whole route renders dynamically** — one uncached fetch poisons the route.
primitives.assumptions: A single uncached fetch forces entire route to render dynamically.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Global route-level failure mode due to local cache policy violation.

layer2.mapping: Represents a failure cascade in GSE’s static rendering pipeline; GSI treats this as a probabilistic risk factor in data integrity models.
layer2.telemetry: Detected through SSR vs ISR metrics in performance tracing.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality in Next.js caching lies between static and dynamic rendering, governed by explicit cache directives and implicit route-level poisoning. In the previous model, caching is granular at the route segment level, controlled via `export const revalidate` and `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate, tags } })`. The Cache Components model introduces a new abstraction layer using `'use cache'` directive, enabling caching of any async operation including database queries and third-party API calls. This shift changes how data dependencies are tracked and invalidated—tags become central to managing cache coherence. The failure mode occurs when a single fetch opts out of caching (`revalidate: 0` or `cache: 'no-store'`), causing the whole route to become dynamic. This is a global degradation that propagates across components and affects both GSE's rendering engine and GSI's probabilistic data models. The caching regime determines whether data flows are deterministic (static) or stochastic (dynamic), influencing downstream inference accuracy and system resource allocation.
